blocks.text: Mastering your Mac environment for Zoom

Project coordinators often juggle multiple apps while on a call. You might have Jira open in one window, a status report in Notion, and your meeting in Zoom. Keeping this organized is vital. Use Mission Control to manage your workspaces. Press ⌃ ↑ to see your open windows. Drag your Zoom window to a dedicated space. This keeps your other tools accessible without cluttering the screen.

Permissions are a common hurdle on macOS. If your camera or microphone is not working, check System Settings. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera. Ensure Zoom is toggled on. Do the same for Microphone. If you still have trouble, restart the app. A simple quit and reopen often fixes minor glitches.
Essential Zoom keyboard shortcuts for coordinators
Speed matters when you are hosting a meeting. Using your mouse to find the mute button wastes precious seconds. Learn these shortcuts to keep your flow.

items: ⌘ ⇧ A: Mute or unmute your audio.
⌘ ⇧ V: Start or stop your video.
⌘ ⇧ S: Start or stop screen sharing.
⌘ ⇧ H: Show or hide the meeting controls.

blocks.text: Customizing these is easy. Open Zoom, then click zoom.us > Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts. You can map these to keys that feel natural to you. If you forget a shortcut, ask Lazur to list them for you.
How to stay organized during meetings

Coordinators track action items while listening to stakeholders. Do not rely on memory. Keep a notepad or a dedicated app like Things 3 open. If you are typing while on a call, use a quiet keyboard. If you need to dictate notes, use the Lazur dictation feature. Hold fn to start dictating. It captures your thoughts accurately without you needing to type.
If you struggle with meeting fatigue, try to keep your camera at eye level. Use a stand for your MacBook. It makes a difference in your posture and how you appear to the team.
blocks.title: Ergonomics matter

blocks.text: Lazur helps you handle the small tasks that add up. You can ask it to open your calendar, find a specific project link, or set a reminder. It lives in your Mac notch, ready when you hold the shortcut. It does not replace your work, but it helps you move faster.

items: Sharing your entire screen when you only need to share one window. Use the share window feature instead.
Forgetting to update the Zoom client. Check for updates weekly to avoid compatibility issues.
Leaving notifications on during a presentation. Use Focus mode on your Mac to silence alerts.
Not testing your audio before a major client meeting. Run a test meeting to verify your mic and speakers.

blocks.text: When managing large meetings, use the waiting room feature. It gives you control over who enters and when. Go to your Zoom web portal settings to enable this. It prevents interruptions during sensitive discussions. If you are recording meetings, ensure you have enough storage on your Mac. You can change your recording location in the Zoom settings to an external drive if space is low.
What to do when things go wrong

Tech issues happen. If your screen share turns black, check your macOS screen recording permissions. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording. Toggle Zoom on. If the app freezes, use ⌘ ⌥ ⎋ to force quit. Relaunching the app usually resolves the state.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Zoom for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It guides you or points at where you should click.

faq.question: How do I update Zoom on my Mac?
faq.answer: Open the Zoom app, click zoom.us in the menu bar, then select Check for Updates.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs running macOS.

faq.question: Is my screen data private with Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only sees your screen while you hold the shortcut. It does not store screenshots or audio.
